flow.name: flowchart
flow.briefing:
SYNTAX
Diagram
  flow "Title" {              open a flowchart; close it with }

Nodes
  start ID "Label"            terminator (ellipse)
  process ID "Label"          process step; alias: task
  decision ID "Label"         branch point (diamond)
  io ID "Label"               input / output; alias: data
  end ID "Label"              terminator (ellipse)

Edges
  A -> B                      directed edge
  A [Yes] -> B                edge with a caption
  A -> B -> C                 chain
  # comment                   line comment (also //)

RULES
- The file is one `flow "Title" { ... }` block. Nothing may sit outside it.
- An element is `<keyword> <ID> "Label"`, one per line. The ID is short, unique, and never quoted.
- Every ID used in an arrow must be declared above it.
- A decision usually has two outgoing arrows, each with its own caption: `D1 [Yes] -> E1`.

WORKED EXAMPLE
flow "Chart Title" {
  start S1 "Start Process"
  io I1 "Read Input Data"
  process P1 "Execute Algorithm"
  decision D1 "Is Valid?"
  end E1 "Finish"

  S1 -> I1 -> P1 -> D1
  D1 [Yes] -> E1
  D1 [No] -> P1
}

bpmn.name: BPMN 2.0 diagram
bpmn.briefing:
SYNTAX
Diagram
  bpmn "Title" {              open a BPMN 2.0 diagram
  pool ID "Label" {           participant, holds lanes
  lane ID "Label" {           role inside a pool

Events
  start ID "Label"            start event (thin circle)
  msg-start ID "Label"        message start (open envelope)
  timer ID "Label"            timer event (clock)
  end ID "Label"              end event (thick circle)
  msg-end ID "Label"          message end (filled envelope)

Activities
  task ID "Label"             task (rounded rectangle)
  send-task ID "Label"        send task
  recv-task ID "Label"        receive task
  script-task ID "Label"      script task
  user-task ID "Label"        user task

Gateways and data
  gw-ex ID "Label"            exclusive gateway (X)
  gw-para ID "Label"          parallel gateway (+)
  gw-inc ID "Label"           inclusive gateway (O)
  data ID "Label"             data object (document)

Flows
  A -> B                      sequence flow
  A [Yes] -> B                conditional flow
  A -.-> D                    data association (dotted)

RULES
- The file is one `bpmn "Title" { ... }` block.
- Participants are `pool ID "Label" { ... }`; inside a pool, roles are `lane ID "Label" { ... }`; elements are declared inside a lane.
- An element is `<keyword> <ID> "Label"`, one per line, and its ID must be unique across the whole diagram.
- Flows are declared after the pool block, at the top level, and may cross lanes.
- A data object is joined with a dotted association `A -.-> D1`, never with a sequence flow.

WORKED EXAMPLE
bpmn "Vacation Request" {
  pool P1 "Request" {
    lane L1 "Employee" {
      start S1 "Submit request"
      task A1 "Fill vacation form"
      send-task A2 "Send to manager"
    }
    lane L2 "Manager" {
      gw-ex G1 "Approved?"
      end E1 "Done"
    }
    lane L3 "HR" {
      send-task A3 "Record leave"
      data D1 "Request log"
      end E2 "Archived"
    }
  }

  S1 -> A1 -> A2 -> G1
  G1 [Yes] -> A3 -> E2
  G1 [No] -> E1
  A3 -.-> D1
}

org.name: organisational chart
org.briefing:
SYNTAX
Chart
  org "Title" {               open an org chart

Boxes
  role ID "Role" "Name"       role band over a name
  role ID "Role"              role band on its own
  role ID "Role" {            role band over sub-roles
  unit "Sub-role" "Name"      one sub-role, inside a role block

Lines
  A -> B                      B reports to A
  A -> B -> C                 chain of reporting lines
  A -.-> B                    advisory tie (dashed)
  # comment                   line comment (also //)

RULES
- The file is one `org "Title" { ... }` block.
- A box is `role ID "ROLE" "Name"`. Drop the second caption for a role with no name attached.
- A box that lists sub-roles opens a block: `role ID "ROLE" { unit "Sub-role" "Name" ... }`. `unit` is only legal inside such a block.
- `A -> B` means B reports to A. Use it once per reporting line.
- `A -.-> B` is an advisory tie, drawn dashed and left out of the reporting bus.

WORKED EXAMPLE
org "FACULTY OF PSYCHOLOGY ORGANISATIONAL CHART" {
  role DEAN "DEAN" "Dr. Marion Hale"
  role SENATE "FACULTY SENATE"

  role VD1 "VICE DEAN I" "Priya Raman, Ph.D"
  role VD2 "VICE DEAN II" "Dr. Elena Sorbo, M.Ed"
  role VD3 "VICE DEAN III" "Tomas Weller, Ph.D"

  role LABS "HEAD OF LABORATORIES" {
    unit "Psychodiagnostics Lab" "Ines Fabri, M.Sc"
    unit "Computing Lab" "Karel Sandvik, M.Sc"
    unit "Experimental and Media Lab" "Ada Moreau, M.Sc"
  }
  role UG "HEAD OF UNDERGRADUATE PROGRAMME" "Nadia Brenner, M.Sc"
  role PG "HEAD OF MASTER PROGRAMME" "Dr. Owen Castellan"
  role QA "QUALITY ASSURANCE CHAIR" "Sofia Lindqvist, M.Sc"

  role SERVICES "SERVICES COORDINATOR" "Rafael Duarte, M.A"
  role QA1 "QA TEAM, UNDERGRADUATE" "Hana Oyelaan, M.Sc"
  role QA2 "QA TEAM, MASTER" "Iris Kovak, M.Sc"

  DEAN -> VD1
  DEAN -> VD2
  DEAN -> VD3
  DEAN -> LABS
  DEAN -> UG
  DEAN -> PG
  DEAN -> QA
  UG -> SERVICES
  QA -> QA1
  QA -> QA2
  DEAN -.-> SENATE
}

usecase.name: UML use case diagram
usecase.briefing:
SYNTAX
Diagram
  usecase "Title" {           open a use case diagram
  system S "Name" {           the boundary the use cases stand in

Elements
  actor A "Name"              a stick figure outside the system
  actor A "Name" right        pin it to that side of the boundary
  usecase U "Goal"            an oval, declared inside a system block

Relations
  A -> U                      association: A takes part in U
  include U -> V              U always runs V
  extend V -> U               V adds to U, under a condition
  inherit A -> B              A is a kind of B (hollow head)
  # comment                   line comment (also //)

RULES
- The file is one `usecase "Title" { ... }` block.
- Actors are declared at the top level; use cases go inside `system S "Name" { ... }`.
- `A -> U` is an association and is the only relation written with a bare arrow.
- `include`, `extend` and `inherit` each take one relation: `include U -> V`.
- An actor with no side written takes the left if it starts anything, the right otherwise.

WORKED EXAMPLE
usecase "Bank ATM" {
  actor CUST "Customer"
  actor TECH "ATM Technician"
  actor BANK "Bank" right

  system ATM "Bank ATM" {
    usecase U1 "Check Balances"
    usecase U2 "Deposit Funds"
    usecase U3 "Withdraw Cash"
    usecase U4 "Transfer Funds"
    usecase U5 "Maintenance"
    usecase U6 "Repair"
  }

  CUST -> U1
  CUST -> U2
  CUST -> U3
  CUST -> U4
  TECH -> U5
  TECH -> U6

  U1 -> BANK
  U2 -> BANK
  U3 -> BANK
  U4 -> BANK
  U5 -> BANK
  U6 -> BANK

  include U3 -> U1
}

activity.name: UML activity diagram
activity.briefing:
SYNTAX
Diagram
  activity "Title" {          open an activity diagram
  lane L "Name" {             a partition; it is drawn as a column

Nodes
  initial S1                  the filled dot it starts at; alias: start
  action A1 "Do it"           a rounded box; alias: task
  decision D1                 a branch; guards go on the arrows
  merge M1                    the branches coming back together
  fork F1                     one flow splitting into several
  join J1                     several coming back into one
  object O1 "Invoice"         a value passing along the flow
  final E1                    the bullseye it ends at; alias: end
  flow-final X1               this one branch stops here

Flows
  A -> B                      control flow
  D1 [yes] -> B               a guard on the branch
  A -.-> O1                   object flow (dashed)
  A -> B -> C                 chain

RULES
- The file is one `activity "Title" { ... }` block.
- Partitions are `lane L "Name" { ... }` and are drawn as columns, left to right in the order written.
- Declare every node inside the partition it belongs to, then wire them after or inside.
- A guard belongs on the arrow out of a decision: `D1 [yes] -> A2`.
- A decision has one flow in and several out; a merge has several in and one out.

WORKED EXAMPLE
activity "Client Visit" {
  lane SALES "Sales Person" {
    initial S1
    action A1 "Call client and set up appointment"
    decision D1
    action A4 "Send follow-up letter"
    decision D2
    final E1
  }

  lane CONS "Consultant" {
    action A2 "Prepare a laptop"
    action A3 "Meet with the client"
    action A5 "Create proposal"
    action A6 "Send proposal to client"
  }

  lane TECH "Corporate Technician" {
    action A7 "Prepare a conference room"
  }

  S1 -> A1 -> D1
  D1 [appointment offsite] -> A2
  D1 [appointment onsite] -> A7
  A2 -> A3
  A7 -> A3
  A3 -> A4 -> D2
  D2 [statement of problem] -> A5 -> A6 -> E1
  D2 [no statement of problem] -> E1
}

erd.name: entity relationship diagram
erd.briefing:
SYNTAX
Diagram
  erd "Title" {               open an entity relationship diagram
  entity E "table" {          an entity, with its attributes inside
  weak E "table" {            one that needs its owner to be told apart

Attributes
  "name" "type"               one attribute row
  pk "id" "bigint"            primary key
  fk "owner_id" "bigint"      foreign key; pfk for both
  "email" "varchar" unique    unique
  "closed_at" "date" null     may be missing; drawn as type?

Relations
  A -> B                      one to many, the usual case
  A one -> many B             the crow's foot at each end
  A many -> one B "label"     and what the relation is called
  A -.-> B                    non-identifying (dashed)
  ends                        one, many, one-or-many, zero-or-one

Which columns it joins
  A.id -> B.a_id              leaves that key and meets that one
  left out                    the keys are paired up on their names
  panel                       or set it in Tables, beside the relation

RULES
- The file is one `erd "Title" { ... }` block.
- An entity is `entity ID "table" { ... }`, and every attribute inside it is written in quotes.
- An attribute is `"name" "type"`, optionally opened with `pk`, `fk` or `pfk` and closed with `unique` or `null`.
- A relation is `A one -> many B`; leaving both ends out means one to many.
- The ends are `one`, `many`, `one-or-many` and `zero-or-one`. A dashed arrow is non-identifying.
- Either end may name the column it joins: `PASSENGER.id one -> many BOOKING.passenger_id`. Left out, the primary key is paired with the foreign key named after it.

WORKED EXAMPLE
erd "Airline Booking" {
  entity PASSENGER "passengers" {
    pk "id" "bigint"
    "first_name" "varchar(50)"
    "last_name" "varchar(50)"
    "passport_number" "varchar(20)" unique
    "country_of_residence" "varchar(50)" null
  }

  entity BOOKING "booking" {
    pk "booking_id" "bigint"
    fk "passenger_id" "bigint"
    fk "flight_id" "bigint"
    "status" "varchar(20)"
    "booking_platform" "varchar(20)"
  }

  entity FLIGHT "flights" {
    pk "flight_id" "bigint"
    fk "airline_id" "bigint"
    "departing_gate" "varchar(20)"
    "arriving_gate" "varchar(20)"
  }

  entity AIRLINE "airline" {
    pk "airline_id" "bigint"
    "airline_name" "varchar(50)"
    "country" "varchar(50)"
  }

  weak BAGGAGE "baggage" {
    pk "id" "bigint"
    fk "booking_id" "bigint"
    "weight_in_kg" "decimal(4,2)"
  }

  PASSENGER one -> many BOOKING "makes"
  AIRLINE one -> many FLIGHT "operates"
  FLIGHT one -> many BOOKING "carries"
  BOOKING one -.-> many BAGGAGE "checks in"
}

architecture.name: software architecture diagram
architecture.briefing:
SYNTAX
Components
  architecture "Title" {      open an architecture diagram; close with }
  zone REGION "Name"          outlined region that grows to fit components centred inside it
  client ID "Name"            place a client component
  service ID "Name"           place a service component
  database ID "Name"          place a database component
  storage ID "Name"           place a storage component
  queue ID "Name"             place a queue component
  cloud ID "Name"             place a cloud component
  external ID "Name"          place a external component
  at 120 200                  optional starting position; nearby nodes align when generated
  size 300 180                component size, or the minimum size of a zone

Connections
  A -> B                      directed data flow; chain as A -> B -> C
  A -.-> B                    dashed event or async flow
  A [request] -> B            caption on a connection

RULES
- The file is one `architecture "Title" { ... }` block.
- Declare components with unique IDs. Optional `at x y` and `size width height` may follow the label in either order. `at` suggests a starting row or column; Generate may move it to leave space.
- Declare zones before their contents; they are independent outlined backdrops, not nested blocks. A component belongs to the smallest original zone containing its centre. With one zone, unplaced components belong to it too. The zone grows or, when unsized, fits its contents.
- Declare all nodes before their connections. `->` is a solid flow; `-.->` is a dashed event.
- Uploaded images belong to the saved sheet, not the source text.

WORKED EXAMPLE
architecture "Recipe Search Platform" {
  zone APP "Recipe Search Platform" at 40 40 size 960 700
  zone SEARCH "Search & discovery" at 270 100 size 290 210
  zone DATA "Recipe management" at 620 100 size 310 320
  zone ACCOUNT "Accounts" at 270 480 size 290 190
  zone MEDIA "Media & files" at 620 480 size 310 190
  client USER "Mobile app" at 70 270
  service FIND "Search engine" at 330 170
  service RECIPE "Recipe service" at 690 160
  database CATALOG "Recipes" at 690 290
  service PROFILE "User profile" at 330 540
  storage FILES "Image storage" at 690 540
  USER -> FIND -> RECIPE -> CATALOG
  USER -> PROFILE
  PROFILE -> FILES
  RECIPE -> FILES
}

class.name: UML class diagram
class.briefing:
SYNTAX
Diagram
  class "Title" {             open a UML class diagram

Classifiers
  class ID "Name" { ... }     class: name, attributes, operations
  abstract ID "Name" { ... }  abstract class, «abstract» over the name
  interface ID "Name" { ... }  interface, «interface» over the name
  enum ID "Name" { ... }      enumeration, «enumeration» over the name
  attr "- name : String"      an attribute, inside the block
  method "+ save() : void"    an operation, inside the block
  value "ACTIVE"              an enumeration literal, inside the block

Relations
  A -> B                      association (plain line)
  A "1" -> "0..*" B "places"  association with multiplicities and a name
  navigate A -> B             directed association (open arrow at B)
  inherit A -> B              generalisation: A is a kind of B
  implement A -> B            realisation: A implements interface B
  aggregate A -> B            aggregation: A has B (hollow diamond at A)
  compose A -> B              composition: A owns B (filled diamond at A)
  depend A -> B               dependency: A uses B (dashed); also A -.-> B
  # comment                   line comment (also //)

RULES
- The file is one `class "Title" { ... }` block.
- A classifier is `class`, `abstract`, `interface` or `enum`, then an ID and its name in quotes. Its block lists `attr` and `method` lines (an enum lists `value` lines); write each member in UML form, e.g. `attr "- name : String"`, `method "+ total() : Decimal"`.
- Visibility is the first character of a member: `+` public, `-` private, `#` protected, `~` package.
- Write a generalisation and a realisation child first: `inherit Cat -> Animal`, `implement Repo -> Store`. They carry no multiplicity.
- Write an aggregation and a composition whole first: `compose Order -> OrderLine`. The diamond is drawn on the whole.
- A bare `A -> B` is an association. Multiplicities are quoted on either side of the arrow and the relation's name follows the second class: `Customer "1" -> "0..*" Order "places"`.

WORKED EXAMPLE
class "Library System" {
  abstract ITEM "LibraryItem" {
    attr "# id : String"
    attr "# title : String"
    method "+ isAvailable() : Boolean"
  }
  class BOOK "Book" {
    attr "- isbn : String"
    attr "- pages : Integer"
    method "+ getAuthor() : Author"
  }
  class MEMBER "Member" {
    attr "- name : String"
    attr "- email : String"
    method "+ borrow(item : LibraryItem) : Loan"
  }
  class LOAN "Loan" {
    attr "- dueDate : Date"
    method "+ isOverdue() : Boolean"
  }
  interface NOTIFY "Notifiable" {
    method "+ notify(message : String) : void"
  }
  enum STATUS "LoanStatus" {
    value "ACTIVE"
    value "RETURNED"
    value "OVERDUE"
  }

  inherit BOOK -> ITEM
  implement MEMBER -> NOTIFY
  MEMBER "1" -> "0..*" LOAN "makes"
  compose LOAN "1" -> "1" STATUS
  LOAN "0..*" -> "1" ITEM "lends"
}

dfd.name: data flow diagram (Gane–Sarson)
dfd.briefing:
SYNTAX
Diagram
  dfd "Title" {               open a data flow diagram (Gane–Sarson)

Shapes
  process ID "Verb + noun"    process, numbered 1, 2, 3 in order written
  process ID "Check stock" "1.2"  process with its own number (level 1)
  entity ID "Name"            external entity: a source or a sink
  store ID "Name"             data store, coded D1, D2, D3 in order written
  store ID "Orders" "D3"      data store with its own code

Flows
  A -> B "Data name"          data flow, named with the data it carries
  A [Data name] -> B          the same, caption in brackets
  # comment                   line comment (also //)

RULES
- The file is one `dfd "Title" { ... }` block, in Gane–Sarson notation.
- Name a process with a verb and a noun (`Validate Order`), an external entity and a data store with a noun.
- Every data flow has a process at one end at least. An entity never connects straight to another entity or to a store, and a store never connects straight to another store.
- Every process has at least one flow in and one flow out: none that only takes data in (a black hole) or only sends it out (a miracle).
- Name every flow with the data it carries: `CUSTOMER -> P1 "Order details"`. A caption in quotes names one flow; a chain takes captions in brackets.
- Processes are numbered 1, 2, 3 and stores coded D1, D2, D3 in the order written; give a process `"1.1"` or a store `"D3"` after its name to set it, as a level-1 diagram does. An entity carries no number.

WORKED EXAMPLE
dfd "Online Shop - Level 0" {
  entity CUST "Customer"
  entity BANK "Bank"
  process P1 "Place Order"
  process P2 "Process Payment"
  process P3 "Ship Order"
  store ORDERS "Orders"
  store STOCK "Inventory"

  CUST -> P1 "Order details"
  P1 -> ORDERS "New order"
  STOCK -> P1 "Stock level"
  P1 -> P2 "Amount due"
  P2 -> BANK "Payment request"
  BANK -> P2 "Payment confirmation"
  P2 -> P3 "Paid order"
  ORDERS -> P3 "Order lines"
  P3 -> STOCK "Stock update"
  P3 -> CUST "Delivery note"
}

state.name: UML state machine diagram
state.briefing:
SYNTAX
Diagram
  state "Title" {             open a UML state machine diagram

States
  initial ID                  initial pseudostate (filled dot); alias: start
  state ID "Name"             state (rounded box)
  state ID "Name" { ... }     state listing its internal activities
  entry "action()"            runs on entering, inside the block
  do "activity()"             runs while in the state, inside the block
  exit "action()"             runs on leaving, inside the block
  final ID                    final state (bullseye); alias: end

Pseudostates
  choice ID                   choice (diamond): branch on guards
  fork ID                     fork bar: one transition into several
  join ID                     join bar: several transitions into one

Transitions
  A -> B                      transition with no trigger (completion)
  A -> B "event [guard] / action"  labelled transition, every part optional
  A -> A "tick"               self-transition
  # comment                   line comment (also //)

RULES
- The file is one `state "Title" { ... }` block.
- Start with one `initial` pseudostate. It leaves by exactly one transition and nothing transitions into it.
- A `final` state ends the machine: no transition leaves it.
- Label a transition `"event [guard] / action"`; any part may be left out, and a transition with no label fires when the state's work is done.
- Branch on guards at a `choice`: one transition in, one out per guard, e.g. `C1 -> PAID "[approved]"`.
- A `fork` takes one transition in and sends several out; a `join` takes several in and sends one out.
- A state's block lists `entry`, `do` and `exit` activities, each at most once, drawn in that order.

WORKED EXAMPLE
state "Order Lifecycle" {
  initial S0
  state NEW "Pending" {
    entry "reserveStock()"
  }
  choice C1
  state PAID "Paid"
  state SHIP "Shipped" {
    entry "notifyCustomer()"
    do "trackParcel()"
  }
  state CANCEL "Cancelled"
  final E1

  S0 -> NEW
  NEW -> C1 "pay"
  C1 -> PAID "[approved]"
  C1 -> CANCEL "[declined] / releaseStock()"
  NEW -> CANCEL "cancel / releaseStock()"
  PAID -> SHIP "dispatch"
  SHIP -> E1 "delivered"
  CANCEL -> E1
}

tree.name: tree diagram
tree.briefing:
SYNTAX
Diagram
  tree "Title" {              open a tree: decision tree, WBS or hierarchy

Boxes
  node ID "Label"             branch: a box with boxes under it
  leaf ID "Label"             leaf (rounded): a path ends here

Branches
  A -> B                      B hangs from A
  A -> B "sunny"              branch with a caption, e.g. a decision's answer
  A -.-> B                    cross link (dashed), outside the hierarchy
  # comment                   line comment (also //)

RULES
- The file is one `tree "Title" { ... }` block.
- Declare every box with `node` (has boxes under it) or `leaf` (ends a path), then hang each from its parent with `A -> B`.
- Every box has exactly one parent, the boxes never loop back, and nothing hangs from a leaf.
- Children are drawn left to right in the order their branches are written.
- A caption on a branch says what leads there: `OUTLOOK -> HUMIDITY "sunny"`.
- `A -.-> B` is a dashed cross link between two boxes the hierarchy has already placed.

WORKED EXAMPLE
tree "Play Outside?" {
  node OUT "Outlook?"
  node HUM "Humidity?"
  node WIND "Windy?"
  leaf Y1 "Play"
  leaf N1 "Don't play"
  leaf Y2 "Play"
  leaf Y3 "Play"
  leaf N2 "Don't play"

  OUT -> HUM "sunny"
  OUT -> Y1 "overcast"
  OUT -> WIND "rain"
  HUM -> N1 "high"
  HUM -> Y2 "normal"
  WIND -> N2 "true"
  WIND -> Y3 "false"
}

sequence.name: UML sequence diagram
sequence.briefing:
SYNTAX
Diagram
  sequence "Title" {          open a sequence diagram

Participants
  object B ":Order"           a named box over a lifeline
  actor A "Customer"          a stick figure
  boundary S "Screen"         what the outside world touches
  control C "Handler"         what runs the work
  entity E "Account"          what is stored
  database D "Ledger"         a store drawn as a drum

Messages
  A -> B "call()"             a call; opens an execution on B
  A ->> B "signal()"          asynchronous, open head
  B --> A "answer"            a reply; ends B's execution
  create A -> B "new"         B's lifeline starts here
  destroy A -> B "close"      B's lifeline ends with a cross
  B -> B "check()"            a call to itself, drawn as a loop

Fragments
  alt "guard" { … }           one section runs
  } else "guard" { … }        the next section of an alt
  opt "guard" { … }           runs only if the guard holds
  loop "while" { … }          runs again and again
  par { … } and { … }         the sections run alongside
  break / critical            the other two operators

Settings
  numbers on                  number every message in order
  activations off             leave the execution bars off
  style tinted                formal, tinted or bold
  colors colorful             or one colour: colors "#2a78d6"
  spacing 150                 least room between two lifelines
  step 46                     from one message down to the next
  text 12                     caption size
  size 700 420                how big it is drawn

RULES
- The file is one `sequence "Title" { ... }` block.
- Declare every participant before the messages, at the top level: `object B ":Order"`.
- Messages are written in the order they are sent, one per line, and that order is the diagram.
- `->` is a call, `->>` is asynchronous, `-->` is a reply. `create` and `destroy` open a message line.
- A fragment is a block: `alt "guard" { ... } else "guard" { ... }`. They may be nested.
- The execution bars are worked out from the messages; never try to place them.

WORKED EXAMPLE
sequence "Shopping Cart" {
  actor CUST "Customer"
  object CART ":Shopping Cart"
  object ORDER ":Order"
  object ITEM ":Item"

  numbers on
  activations on

  CUST -> CART "«create»"
  CART -> ORDER "getTotal()"
  ORDER -> ITEM "getPrice()"
  ITEM --> ORDER "itemPrice"
  ORDER -> ORDER "calculateTotal()"
  ORDER --> CART "totalPrice"
}

bar.name: bar chart
bar.briefing:
SYNTAX
Chart
  bar "Title" {               open a bar chart; close it with }

Readings
  Apples 40                   one bar, named and measured
  "Two words" 40              a name with a space goes in quotes

Bars
  bars horizontal             vertical or horizontal
  layout stacked              grouped or stacked, for several series

Axes
  x "Caption"                 caption under the across axis
  y "Caption"                 caption beside the up axis
  grid value                  none, value, category, both
  range 0 250                 pin where the value axis runs

Look
  colors colorful             auto, single, colorful, warm, cool, ink
  colors "#2a78d6"            one colour, pinned
  style framed                plain, ruled, framed, bold
  legend bottom               auto, none, right, bottom, top
  values on                   write the number on every mark
  size 520 340                how big the chart is drawn
  # comment                   line comment (also //)

RULES
- The file is one `bar "Title" { ... }` block. Nothing may sit outside it.
- A reading is `Name 40`, one per line, and draws a bar per reading. A name with a space or a comma in it goes in quotes.

mind.name: mind map
mind.briefing:
SYNTAX
Map
  mind "Central idea" {       open a mind map; the title is the middle

Branches
  "A branch"                  one branch off the idea
  "A branch" {                a branch with more hanging off it
  "A branch" "#2a78d6"        a branch in a colour of its own
  "A branch" circle           a branch drawn as a different shape

Arrangement
  layout radial               radial, sides, down
  spread 150                  how far a level sits from the one above
  line curve                  curve, elbow, straight
  shape round                 round, pill, box, circle, diamond, hex, none

Look
  colors colorful             auto, single, colorful, warm, cool, ink
  branch on                   one hue per branch, rather than per level
  style formal                formal, soft, bold, wire
  text 13                     how big a caption is set
  size 760 560                how big the map is drawn
  # comment                   line comment (also //)

RULES
- The file is one `mind "Title" { ... }` block. Nothing may sit outside it.
- The title is the idea in the middle; everything else hangs off it.
- A branch is a caption in quotes on its own line. Give it a `{ ... }` block for whatever hangs off it, nested as deep as you like.

- Settings are written as `name value`, in any order.

SYNTAX

  column "3-GEN" "Kaizen"     a column under a spanning group heading
  column "Safety" "" "#2a78d6"  a heading with its own fill

Rows and cells
  row "Amir" "x" "" "Trainer"  one value per column; any text is valid
  row "Budi" {                open a row when cells need their own colours
  cell "High" "#00a86b"       one cell value and an optional fill
  color "#fff2cc"             the row heading's own fill, inside a row block

Arrangement
  header vertical             horizontal or vertical column labels
  align center                left, center, right
  row-header 140              width of the headings down the left

Look

  row-color "#dce9f8"         shared row-heading colour
  cell-color "#fff2cc"        body fill for bands or a heatmap
  grid-color "#1f2933"        lines and the title

  text 13                     caption size
  size 760 460                how big the matrix is drawn
  # comment                   line comment (also //)

RULES
- The file is one `matrix "Title" { ... }` block. Nothing may sit outside it.
- Declare columns first with `column "Name"`; an optional second caption groups consecutive columns under one spanning heading.

- When cells need colours, open a row block and write each as `cell "anything" "#rrggbb"`. The colour is optional and the value remains text.

- Settings are written as `name value`, in any order.

prisma.name: PRISMA 2020 flow diagram
prisma.briefing:
SYNTAX
Diagram
  prisma "Title" {            open a PRISMA 2020 flow diagram
  band "Identification"       name the phase the rows after it stand in

The flow
  row "Records screened" 955  a step and its total
  row "Records identified from" 1423 {  a step with lines under it
  "Databases" 1200            one line and its own count
  side "Records excluded" 812 {  what left the flow at the row above
  "Duplicate records removed" 300  one reason and its count

Look
  style formal                formal, banded, bold
  bands on                    the four phase bands down the left
  text 12                     caption size
  size 820 660                how big the flow is drawn
  # comment                   line comment (also //)

RULES
- The file is one `prisma "Title" { ... }` block. Nothing may sit outside it.
- The title is the name of the flow, written above it.
- A `band` names the phase every row after it stands in, until the next `band`. Consecutive rows naming the same band share one strip, so Screening may cover two rows.
- A step is `row "Caption" 955`, optionally followed by a `{ ... }` block of lines. Each line is `"Caption" 1200`.
- A `side` box follows the row it belongs to and says what left the flow there. It takes the same caption, total and block.
- Counts are written plainly and drawn as `(n = 955)`. Leave the number out to draw the caption on its own.
- Settings are written as `name value`, in any order.
- Do not invent settings. Every one the language has is listed above.

WORKED EXAMPLE
prisma "PRISMA 2020 flow diagram" {
  band "Identification"
  row "Records identified from" 1423 {
    "Databases" 1200
    "Registers" 223
  }
  side "Records removed before screening" 468 {
    "Duplicate records removed" 300
    "Records marked as ineligible by automation tools" 100
    "Records removed for other reasons" 68
  }

  band "Screening"
  row "Records screened" 955
  side "Records excluded" 812
  row "Reports sought for retrieval" 143
  side "Reports not retrieved" 20

  band "Eligibility"
  row "Reports assessed for eligibility" 123
  side "Reports excluded" 110 {
    "Reason 1" 50
    "Reason 2" 35
    "Reason 3" 25
  }

  band "Included"
  row "Studies included in review" 13 {
    "Reports of included studies" 16
  }
}

quadrant.briefing:

Axes

  y "Impact" "Low" "High"     up axis: its name, then its low and high ends

Quarters

  top-right "Major projects"  caption of the top-right quarter
  bottom-left "Fill-ins"      caption of the bottom-left quarter
  bottom-right "Thankless tasks"  caption of the bottom-right quarter

Items

Look

  color "#2a78d6"             the colour every item takes
  text 13                     caption size, 9 to 22
  size 560 500                width and height on the sheet

RULES
- The file is one `quadrant "Title" { ... }` block. Nothing may sit outside it.
- Write each axis as its name and then the words at its low and high ends: `x "Effort" "Low" "High"`. The low end of the up axis is at the bottom.

quadrant "Feature Priorities" {

  bottom-left "Fill-ins"

  item "Legacy importer" 78 18
}

gantt.name: Gantt chart
gantt.briefing:
SYNTAX
Chart
  gantt "Title" {             open a Gantt chart
  unit "Week"                 what one numbered unit is called
  today 5                     a dashed line through the unit the chart is read in

Tasks
  section "Research"          a section; the tasks after it are listed under it
  task T1 "Survey" 1 3        starts in unit 1, lasts 3 units
  task T2 "Write" after T1 2  starts once T1 ends, lasts 2
  task T3 "Test" after T1 T2 2  starts once both have ended
  task T1 "Survey" 1 3 done 60  60% of it done
  milestone M1 "Defence" after T2  a diamond where T2 ends
  milestone M2 "Launch" 12    a diamond at the start of unit 12

Look
  color "#2a78d6"             the colour every bar takes
  text 12                     caption size, 9 to 20
  size 760 400                width and height on the sheet

RULES
- The file is one `gantt "Title" { ... }` block. Nothing may sit outside it.
- Time is counted in whole units from 1 (week 1, week 2, …); `unit` only says what a unit is called.
- A task is `task ID "Name"`, then either the unit it starts in or `after` the IDs it waits for, then how many units it lasts. It may end with `done` and a percentage.
- A milestone is `milestone ID "Name"` then a unit or `after` IDs; it lasts nothing and takes no `done`.
- `section "Name"` lists every task after it under that section, until the next section.
- Every ID after `after` is a task or milestone in the chart, and following them never loops back.
- Settings are written as `name value`, in any order.
- Do not invent settings. Every one the language has is listed above.

WORKED EXAMPLE
gantt "Thesis Schedule" {
  unit "Week"
  today 5

  section "Proposal"
  task T1 "Literature review" 1 3 done 100
  task T2 "Write the proposal" after T1 2 done 60
  milestone M1 "Proposal defence" after T2

  section "Research"
  task T3 "Build the prototype" after M1 4
  task T4 "Collect the data" after T3 3
  task T5 "Analyse the results" after T4 2

  section "Writing"
  task T6 "Write chapters 4 and 5" after T5 3
  milestone M2 "Final defence" after T6
}
